transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that I've just gotten... really slowed down lately. I'm an auditor, and it's gotten to the point where I can just sit there staring at one audit workpaper for twenty minutes before I even move my hand to type. People at work have actually started noticing that I'm not keeping up, so... I figured I needed to come in.
Along with this slowing down, have you noticed feeling sad, down, or depressed most of the day?

Yes, I have. Most days I just... I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It really just feels like the day is already lost before I've even gotten out of bed. So, yeah, I've definitely been feeling down most of the time.

Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and were more talkative or impulsive than normal?

No... I haven't ever had anything like that. I don't really get bursts of energy or feel overly happy, and I definitely haven't had times where I needed less sleep. It's pretty much just been the exact opposite of that. So, no, I haven't had a period like you're describing.
Have you noticed any other physical changes recently, such as feeling unusually cold, gaining weight, or having dry skin or hair?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, my weight has been pretty much the same as always, and... I don't feel unusually cold or anything. My skin and hair seem normal to me. So, no, no changes like that.
Have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things that others don't see, or having beliefs that others find unusual or hard to believe?

Actually, yes... I have. It happens when I'm working. Sometimes when I open a spreadsheet or check my email, I hear a voice. It's a really clear voice, and it sounds like it's coming from just behind my laptop. It says, "You missed it, they know." And... there's no one else in the room when it happens. It's just me. But I hear it plain as day.
Does this voice only happen during the times when you're feeling down and slowed down, or have you ever heard it even when your mood felt normal?

It only happens when I'm feeling down. I never heard that voice... or believed the firm was secretly building a case against me before this depression settled in. None of that happened back when I felt normal. Those experiences really only started after my mood and energy had already been low for a while.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression like this in the past, at any point before this current one?

No, I haven't. I mean, I've had bad days or stressful weeks before, especially during tax season, but... nothing like this. This is the first time I've ever felt this low and... had these things happen. So, no, never anything like this in the past.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a first-ever major depressive episode characterized by pervasive depressed mood, marked psychomotor retardation (staring at work for 20 minutes without acting), and functional decline at work. During this episode, he developed mood-congruent psychotic features—an auditory hallucination reflecting themes of guilt/failure ('You missed it, they know')—which emerged only after and during the depressive episode, with no psychotic symptoms present at baseline or premorbidly. No manic/hypomanic episodes were reported, ruling out bipolar disorder with psychotic features. No physical/endocrine symptoms (weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin) suggest hypothyroid-induced mood/psychotic symptoms. The temporal relationship (psychosis strictly confined to the depressive episode) supports a primary mood disorder with psychotic features rather than a schizoaffective or independent psychotic disorder. This is consistent with Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, Severe, with Psychotic Features (F32.3).
